text:
Sophie: Heads-up — seeing a flurry of gpu_unhealthy alerts from dcgm-exporter in us-west-2. Looks like a lot of short-lived Xid/ECC spikes. Anyone on-call who can triage?
Omar: I noticed ~6 nodes flipped in the last 2 hours, mostly transient Xid=13 and small ECC corrected increases. Alerts firing on a single sample atm.
Lia: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd/gpu-health?orgId=1 — you can see the bursts. Exporter scrape is 5s, Prom rule is currently `expr: gpu_unhealthy > 0` with `for: 1m`. Seems too sensitive.
Kevin: Proposal: make the alert require sustained signal, e.g. require 2 consecutive evals or bump `for` to 3m. Also consider increasing exporter scrape to 15s to reduce noise, but that impacts latency for some jobs.
Morgan: We can't globally change exporter scrape; some latency-sensitive workloads expect 5s. Alternative: change Prom rule to use avg_over_time or count_over_time instead of raw instant >0. That keeps exporter fast but reduces false positives.
Sophie: Suggested prom rule snippet:```
- alert: GPUCardUnhealthy
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_unhealthy[3m]) > 0.0
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/gpu-unhealthy
```
DevOpsBot: prometheus-apply: PR created by @Lia -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/4123 (changes to alert rule).
Omar: Also thinking about k8s behavior — autoscaler sometimes kills nodes mid-flap. Can we add a node annotation like `gpu.redwood/drain-safety=transient` to defer termination for flapping cards? Update the drain playbook to only drain after Xid/ECC exceed persistent thresholds.
Lia: I'll add a short runbook blurb and a canary change. For now I'll mute the noisy alert with a 30m silence in Alertmanager while we test the new rule. :thumbsup: 
Kevin: If we silence, create a ticket to revert if things get worse. Also create a Grafana alert for "card flapping rate" (rate of transitions) so we still catch real failures.
Morgan: Action items: (1) PR merged for prom rule (Lia), (2) canary exporter scrape tweak on 1 node (Kevin), (3) annotation + drain playbook update (Omar), (4) alertmanager silence + revert ticket (Sophie). I'll open INFRA-789 to track.
Sophie: Thanks — schedule canary rollout tonight at 22:00 PST. I'll post updates here. If the rule change suppresses real failures we’ll revert and run a root-cause. @DevOpsBot please schedule.
DevOpsBot: Scheduled: prom-rule-rollout at 22:00 PST. Notification will post to #eng-infra at rollout time.
